sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 (2001)
cleanIntro: The regular clean leaves the rifle in one piece: the bore and the chamber with the bolt held back, then the outside. Deep Clean is the only taking-apart Remington prints for this rifle: the fore-end off to reach the action spring and tube, and the trigger plate assembly out on its two pins. The barrel, the bolt and the gas parts stay where they are.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, red band out of sight
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction and keep your finger out of the trigger guard. Push the button behind the trigger until you cannot see its red band. Red showing means the rifle will fire.
steps.prose: Some rifles have a J-shaped key slot in that button. If the button is locked, unlock it with its key. Do not force the key, and never poke the slot with anything else. Keep all ammunition off the bench.
steps.aside: If you lose the key, DO NOT attempt to disengage the safety mechanism using a foreign object. This will damage your firearm.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, push the button so that the RED BAND MARKING CANNOT BE SEEN.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — The Safety Mechanism, printed p.7; The Security System, printed p.8
steps.warn: Even when the safety mechanism is engaged, careless handling can cause the firearm to fire.

steps.title: Magazine latch forward, magazine out
steps.action: Push the magazine latch forward, toward the muzzle, and pull the magazine down out of the rifle.
steps.prose: Magazine first. Work the bolt with a loaded magazine still in and you will feed another round. An empty magazine well says nothing about the chamber.
steps.quote: Push the magazine latch forward and pull the magazine from the firearm.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Unload the Firearm, step 3, printed p.10; Picture 7, printed p.9

steps.title: Handle back: the chambered round comes out
steps.action: Pull the operating handle all the way back so a cartridge in the chamber comes out of the ejection port. Keep your hand out of the port.
steps.prose: With the magazine out there is nothing to hold the bolt back, so it runs forward when you let go. Keep hold of the handle.
steps.quote: Pull the operating handle rearward to remove the cartridge from the chamber.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Unload the Firearm, step 4, printed p.10

steps.title: Empty the magazine, then hold the bolt back on it
steps.action: Away from the rifle, push each cartridge forward and out of the magazine until it is empty. Put the empty magazine back in and pull the handle fully rearward until the follower holds the bolt open.
steps.prose: The empty magazine is what holds this rifle open, so it stays in while you clean. The small bolt release at the bottom of the receiver lets the bolt go; keep fingers off it until you mean to use it.
steps.aside: Pull the operating handle fully rearward until the bolt is held open by the magazine follower.
steps.quote: Remove the cartridges from the magazine.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Unload the Firearm, steps 5–6, printed p.10; The Barrel, I, step 3, printed p.9

steps.title: Look and feel, chamber and magazine
steps.action: Look through the ejection port into the chamber and down at the empty follower. Then feel the chamber with a fingertip.
steps.prose: Two places, two looks. Remington prints this check at the head of every cleaning job in the book.
steps.quote: Look into the ejection port. Check the chamber and magazine to make sure there are no cartridges in the firearm.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — The Barrel, I, WARNING, printed p.9

steps.title: The rifle stays whole for this clean
steps.action: No screw or pin comes out for the regular clean. Push a cleaning rod in at the muzzle and all the way through until you see it in the ejection port. That proves the bore is open.
steps.prose: If something is stuck, tap it lightly with the rod from the muzzle. If it will not push out easily, it goes to the factory or a gunsmith Remington recommends.
steps.quote: Insert a cleaning rod into the muzzle. Push the rod completely through the barrel until the rod can be seen in the ejection port.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — The Barrel, I, step 4, and II, printed p.9
steps.warn: Never try to remove an object from the barrel by loading another cartridge and firing.

steps.title: Wet brush, muzzle to chamber
steps.action: Eye protection on. Fit a brush of the right caliber to the rod and wet it with gun cleaning solvent. Push it through the barrel several times, going in at the muzzle.
steps.prose: The barrel does not come off in this book, so the muzzle is the way in. Keep the rod centered and off the crown, and push the brush all the way out before you bring it back.
steps.quote: Always clean the barrel from the muzzle to the chamber.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Barrel, steps 2–4 and NOTE, printed p.11

steps.title: A new patch each pass, until one is clean
steps.action: Take the brush off and fit the tip with a patch of the right size. Push patches through, a new one every time, until one comes out clean.
steps.prose: A patch used twice only carries the dirt back in.
steps.quote: Repeat several times using a new cleaning patch each time, until the patch is not dirty.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Barrel, steps 5–6, printed p.11

steps.title: Oiled patch, then a dry one
steps.action: Push one clean patch soaked with Rem Oil through the barrel, then a clean, dry patch to take the extra out. Look through the bore before you put the rod away.
steps.prose: Do not skip the dry patch. Oil left standing in a rifle bore raises pressure on the next shot.
steps.quote: Push a clean, dry patch through the barrel to remove excess lubricant.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Barrel, steps 7–8, printed p.11
steps.warn: After cleaning, make sure the barrel is free of obstructions.

steps.title: Chamber brush, in through the port
steps.action: Safety on, bolt held back by the follower. Wet the chamber brush with solvent, push it into the chamber through the ejection port, and repeat several times.
steps.prose: Remington supplied a chamber brush with this rifle. A bore brush is too small to scrub the chamber walls, and a dirty chamber is where a case sticks.
steps.aside: Use the chamber brush that comes with the firearm.
steps.quote: Push the brush into the chamber through the ejection port.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Chamber, steps 1–4, printed p.12

steps.title: Chamber dried with patches
steps.action: Put a patch on the rear end of the chamber brush and dry the chamber. Use a clean patch each time until one comes out clean.
steps.prose: The chamber is left dry, with no oil in it. Look down the bore once more: no bristle, no patch, nothing left behind.
steps.quote: Repeat using a clean patch each time, until patch is not dirty.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Chamber, step 5 and WARNING, printed p.12; Lubrication and Maintenance, printed p.11

steps.title: Outside: a thin coat, and no more
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the barrel and the outside metal with a thin coat of Rem Oil on a soft, clean cloth.
steps.prose: For storage, clean it carefully and oil it thoroughly. Before you use it again, take all the extra oil off and wipe the chamber and bore fully dry.
steps.quote: Over-lubrication should be avoided at all times.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — Lubrication and Maintenance, printed p.11; To Clean the Barrel, step 9, printed p.11
steps.warn: Excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could adversely affect the function and safe operation of your firearm.

steps.title: Look it over, and know when it is due
steps.action: With the bolt held back, look over the bore, the bolt face and as much of the inside as you can see. You want it clean, with no rust and no grit. Clean the bore each time you are going to shoot, and the whole rifle before and after long storage and at least once a year.
steps.prose: If anything is worn or damaged, or it has not worked right, stop using it and have it checked by Remington or a gunsmith Remington recommends.
steps.aside: Remington recommends that you have your firearm professionally serviced annually.
steps.quote: Periodically inspect the internal workings of your firearm to be sure they’re clean and free of rust, unwanted dirt and debris.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — 9th Commandment, printed p.6; maintenance and care, printed p.16
steps.warn: So never alter or modify your firearm in any way.

deepSteps.title: Unloaded, safety on, finger away
deepSteps.action: Eye protection on. Push the safety button until the red band is out of sight. Check the chamber and the magazine, by eye and by fingertip: no cartridges anywhere.
deepSteps.prose: The safety stays on and the trigger stays untouched for the whole job. The hammer is cocked when the trigger plate comes out.
deepSteps.quote: Make sure there are no cartridges in the magazine or chamber.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly, WARNING and step 1, printed p.12; Picture 18, printed p.12
deepSteps.warn: Never pull the trigger when the safety mechanism is engaged.

deepSteps.title: Bolt released forward, magazine out
deepSteps.action: Keep your fingers away from the ejection port and the operating handle. Push the bolt release to close the action. Then push the magazine latch forward and pull the magazine out.
deepSteps.prose: The action is closed for this whole job. The bolt runs home hard on its spring.
deepSteps.quote: Keep your fingers away from the ejection port and operating handle.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Remove the Magazine, steps 3–5, printed p.9; To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly, step 2, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Fore-end screw out, fore-end off
deepSteps.action: Loosen the screw at the front end of the fore-end and take the fore-end off.
deepSteps.prose: The parts list shows a cap and a spacer at the front of the fore-end. Keep them with it, in order. Nothing else at the front of the rifle comes off.
deepSteps.quote: Loosen the fore-end screw and remove the fore-end.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Action Spring and Action Tube, step 1, printed p.12; parts list, printed pp.14–15

deepSteps.title: Action spring and tube, cleaned in place
deepSteps.action: Brush the action spring and the action tube with gun cleaning solvent. Dry them with a clean cloth.
deepSteps.prose: The spring stays on its tube. The book has no step for taking either one off.
deepSteps.quote: Brush action spring and action tube with gun cleaning solvent.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Action Spring and Action Tube, steps 2–3, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Thin oil on the spring and tube
deepSteps.action: Put a thin coat of Rem Oil on the action spring and the action tube.
deepSteps.prose: Thin means a film you can feel but that does not run. It is there against rust.
deepSteps.quote: Apply a thin coat of Rem™ Oil to prevent rusting.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Action Spring and Action Tube, step 4, printed p.12

deepSteps.title: Two trigger plate pins, tapped out
deepSteps.action: Action closed, safety on. Tap the front and rear trigger plate pins out of the receiver with a punch that fits them.
deepSteps.prose: Support the receiver so the taps move the pin and not the rifle. Front and rear are listed as separate parts, so lay them down in order.
deepSteps.quote: Tap out front and rear trigger plate pins.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly, steps 1–3, printed p.12; parts list, printed p.15

deepSteps.title: Rear of the plate up, then out
deepSteps.action: Lift the rear of the trigger plate assembly first, then take the assembly out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Remington's picture shows the rifle upside down, so the plate lifts up and away. The strip ends here: the assembly is not taken apart.
deepSteps.quote: Lift rear of the trigger plate assembly and remove the assembly from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly, step 4 and Picture 16, printed p.12
deepSteps.warn: All adjustments to the trigger and trigger plate assembly must be made by the factory or a REMINGTON® AUTHORIZED GUNSMITH.

deepSteps.title: The trigger plate, cleaned as one unit
deepSteps.action: Spray the assembly with Rem Oil, let it stand for 15 minutes, spray it again to wash it off, then shake off the extra.
deepSteps.prose: Keep it whole and keep your finger off the trigger. The hammer is cocked, with nothing to stop it.
deepSteps.aside: Let stand for 15 minutes. Spray again to wash off components. Shake off excess lubricant.
deepSteps.quote: Spray the trigger plate assembly with Rem™ Oil as shown.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for Model 7400 Autoloading Centerfire Rifle — Form RD 7056 Rev. Orig 4-01 — To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly, NOTE, step 5 and WARNING, printed p.12
deepSteps.warn: Excessive use of a non-recommended lubricant could adversely affect the function and safe operation of your firearm.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Bolt held back by the empty magazine, chamber checked again
Wet brush through several times, muzzle to chamber
Patches, a new one each pass, until one is clean
One oiled patch, then one dry patch
⛔ Bore looked through: nothing left in it

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush wet with solvent, in through the ejection port, several times
Dried with clean patches on the rear of the brush
⛔ No oil left in the chamber

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE AND STORAGE
tasks: Outside metal wiped with a thin coat of oil
Before storage: cleaned carefully and oiled thoroughly
Before use after storage: extra oil off, chamber and bore dry

reassembly: ⛔ Check again: no cartridges in the chamber or the magazine. Eye protection on.
Fore-end back on, and tighten the fore-end screw. The book prints no torque figure.
Look at the left side of the trigger plate assembly: the end of the disconnector must be below the end of the left connector. ⛔ If it is not, do not put the assembly in.
Put the trigger plate assembly carefully into the receiver. If it does not go in easily, take it back out and check the disconnector again.
Line up the holes, then tap in the front and rear trigger plate pins.
⛔ Safety on, red band out of sight.
Empty magazine in, pushed up until it is fully latched.
fncheck: No ammunition near the rifle, safety on with the red band hidden, empty magazine latched in. Pull the operating handle fully rearward: the follower holds the bolt open. Keep your fingers clear of the port and the handle, and push the bolt release: the bolt closes. Open it once more, look into the chamber, and leave it open and unloaded. The book prints no other check, and this one never asks you to pull the trigger.
reassemblyRoutine: Nothing was taken apart, so nothing goes back together.
⛔ Check the chamber, the bore and the magazine: no cartridges, no patch, no brush. Safety on, red band out of sight.
To close it, keep your fingers away from the ejection port and the operating handle, and push the bolt release.
Push the magazine latch forward to take the empty magazine out, or leave it latched in and the action open.
